Senses.Explanation: 劫外 means beyond the cosmic aeon. Dongshan Liangjie writes of a withered tree flowering in spring beyond the aeon, while Zhongfeng Mingben writes of spring returning beyond the aeon. Senses.Explanation: 呈漆器 means present the lacquerware. Asked what it is like when people of the Way meet, Zhaozhou answers, 'Present the lacquerware.' Xueguan Zhiyin later treats speaking as sharing Zhaozhou's presentation of lacquerware, contrasted with Vimalakirti's silence. Lingshu Yuan raises the exchange and praises its object as all-sided, self-turning, and open in every direction. These receptions make the phrase a recognizable Zhaozhou formula, but do not justify translating away its lacquerware image. Yuan'an Liao applies the same words directly when a monk presents his sitting cloth, confirming that the formula can be turned onto an observable presentation.
